title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster.
source_locator: Results, 'Activation of DNp09 neurons induced freezing' and 'Freezing probability upon DNp09 activation depended on speed'; Fig. 6b-g; Methods 'Optogenetic activation'
quote: We found that CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki 2018 name DNp09 with split line SS01540 (SS1540); the kit lists SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS (DNp09;DNp71) and 'DNp09' is also a hemibrain synonym of DNp71, so the MANC type with the same Namiki name, DNp09, is chosen at medium confidence.
stimulation: 627 nm red LEDs, 0.025 mW/mm2, 10 repetitions of 2 s on / 20 s off; also closed-loop 2 s pulses triggered at low (<1 mm), high (>7.5 mm) or very high (>10 mm displacement per 500 ms) speeds
sensory_condition: freely moving in 30 mm (open loop) or 60 mm (closed loop) arenas, infrared backlight; controls raised without retinal
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (cells not named; paper refers to FlyLight page for SS01540)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of stimulation events; closed loop: 85% (506/593) at low speed, 55% (223/403) at very high speed
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed test flies, 72 controls (open loop); 50 per speed condition in closed loop
notes: Main outcome is freezing (complete immobility scored from pixel change; no leg tracking), so legs coded 'no' and effect 'stops' (PROTOCOL 3). Freezing was preceded by a brief rise in walking speed ('The lag in freezing correlated with an initial increase in walking speed, induced by DNp09 activation'; Discussion: 'DNp09-induced freezing was always preceded by running'). In Fig. 6d the baseline speed was about 10 mm/s and the speed spike lasted well under 1 s, i.e. a speed-up in flies that were mostly already walking (PROTOCOL 3: speed change, not coded as rhythm). Flies stimulated at low speed (<2 mm/s) mostly froze. Jumps at light offset. Paper also cites Cande et al. 2018 (running then pausing; 15 s stimulation led to sustained immobility), which is not coded here.
